result.reviewScopeSummary: Follow-up verification focused on the two prior blockers: the archive read service’s handling of throwing provenance lookups and the Story 6 degradation proof in `archive-api.test.ts`, then re-ran the targeted suite plus the configured story and epic gates.

priorFindingStatuses.rationale: `DefaultArchiveReadService` now degrades lookup failures instead of rejecting the archive read: artifact version fetches are caught per version (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/archive-read.service.ts:96-104`), process/source provenance list calls are wrapped in fallback loaders (`:113-123`, `:231-266`), and the server tests now prove a throwing source lookup and a throwing artifact lookup still return HTTP 200 with the unaffected entry ready and the affected entry degraded (`tests/service/server/archive-api.test.ts:527-612`).

`TC-6.3b` no longer seeds a pre-degraded canonical row. It now uses `ThrowingArtifactVersionLookupStore` with a ready `processEventArchiveEntryFixture`, asserts the archive page still returns 200, asserts the affected entry becomes degraded at read time, and asserts no `relatedArtifactProvenance` is exposed on the failed lookup path (`tests/service/server/archive-api.test.ts:567-609`). That satisfies the story anti-shim requirement to fail the actual enrichment dependency rather than fabricating a degraded response.

additionalObservations: The added source-lookup-failure test is not named as a TC, but it closes the anti-shim proof point by failing the real enrichment dependency while preserving unrelated archive entries on the same page.
`verify-all` passed after the fix, so the Story 6 convergence work did not regress the broader archive, turn, or derived-view surfaces.
